extracted.intended_audience: general French-speaking readers interested in travel, colonial society, agriculture, and education (late 19th century)
extracted.subtask_description: A late-19th-century French travelogue chapter describing social, agricultural, educational, industrial and institutional practices in New Zealand (Wellington, Christchurch, Canterbury). Contains observations and prescriptive remarks about schooling, farming, insurance, industry and public institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education pedagogy: practice over theory
rubrics_metrics.description: «Dans les sciences, on donne peu de temps à la théorie et beaucoup à la pratique dans les laboratoires.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for teaching by doing: more laboratory/practical hours than theoretical instruction; practical training produces better immediate results in applied sciences and agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language instruction by conversation manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: «le latin est enseigné en trois ans, comme on enseigne les autres langues vivantes au moyen de manuels de conversation.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach living languages using conversation manuals for faster acquisition; Latin still taught but modern languages benefit from oral-conversation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual aids (tableaux, albums) to accelerate learning
rubrics_metrics.description: «Par les tableaux on apprend, autant et plus vite, par les yeux... Aux États-Unis, j'avais remarqué les albums de géographie qui, en quelques semaines, au moyen des yeux, peuvent apprendre aux enfants ce qu'il nous faut des années...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage schools and committees to examine the best educational visual materials used abroad (Germany, England, America) and adopt them; visual instruction can drastically shorten learning time for subjects like geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: School quality measured by enrollment numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: «Tout ce qu'on lui demande chaque année, c'est le nombre d'élèves qui fréquentent son école.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this colonial context, inspectors/directors evaluate school performance primarily by pupil attendance counts rather than credentials; emphasis on measurable enrollment as a key metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-supported school funding via reserved land revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: «Dans tout établissement nouveau, le gouvernement retient une partie de terres qu'il loue et en affecte les revenus aux écoles.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reserved public land yields to finance educational institutions; land improvement increases long-term school revenues and funds teacher salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-sectarian public schooling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: «On a donc abstenu [d'enseigner la religion], laissant le soin de cet enseignement à la famille et aux divers clergés.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid sectarian conflict in a plural religious environment, public instruction omits formal religion classes; religious instruction is delegated to families and religious bodies, with religious communities founding their own schools when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farm-school curriculum and workload (Canterbury farm school)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed weekly allocation of time and practical activities at the farm school: total 40 hours of work per week plus study; subjects and hours enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit breakdown: agriculture lessons 2h; manual farm/laitage work 17h; chemistry lessons 2h + lab 3.5h; natural sciences lessons 2h + lab 1.5h; mathematics lessons 4h; veterinary science 1h; horticulture 2.5h; farrier/locksmith 1h; carpentry/joinery 1.5h; exams 2h; (total 40h) plus additional practical duties in later years (plan surveys, bookkeeping). Course length ~3 years; emphasis on hands-on training (milking, butter/cheese making, ploughing, fertiliser composition, shearing, shoeing horses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical vocational training produces competent farmers
rubrics_metrics.description: «Passant ainsi de la théorie à la pratique, ils ne peuvent devenir que d'excellents fermiers...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that combining limited theory with extensive practical farm work yields graduates suited to colonial agricultural labour markets where manual skill is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meat-preserving technology preference: compressed-air refrigeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of Wellington meat preserving Co.'s system: compressed air refrigeration preferred to ether evaporation; machine compresses air into cold chambers, freezes carcasses; cheaper and simpler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compressed-air refrigeration is recommended as more economical and simpler than ether-based evaporation methods; operational notes include process flow (chambers for 300 sheep, 24-hour freezing before shipping), use of ship's propulsion engine to power compressors, and cost metrics (cost of freezing & freight = 4 pence/lb; sale price in London 6 pence/lb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government life assurance model characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Government provides life insurance at lower premiums, guarantees payment from revenues, shares entire profit among insured, loans against policies at 7% up to 90% of policy value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete premium comparisons by age and sums insured are given; the model increases accessibility (sold at post offices and stations), builds large reserve funds, and distributes bonuses to policyholders (example: first five-year bonus figures). Encourages saving via daily small payments to secure survivors' start-up capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: School hygiene and daily habits (bathing)
rubrics_metrics.description: «Les élèves ici, comme dans tous les pays anglais, ont l'habitude du bain ou douche journalière.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote daily bathing routines at boarding/educational institutions for health and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison labour as cost-saving and constructive measure
rubrics_metrics.description: «Les prisonniers sont employés à charrier et à empiler eux-mêmes les briques pour construire leur cage. C'est sage et économique.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inmate labour for construction and material production to reduce costs and provide useful work, while acknowledging moral judgment as expressed by the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural land management: paddock rotation and drainage
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice: divide land into paddocks; rotate stock between paddocks to allow grass to regrow quickly; drain alluvial plains to turn them into highly productive farmland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paddock system leads to rapid fattening of sheep; drained alluvial soils yield high returns (20–80 to 1 in wheat; 16–20 tonnes potatoes/acre). Promotes conversion from wheat to pasture when facing international competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonial economic strategy for French emigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice: 'Le Français, s'il veut être de son temps, doit semer le blé en Amérique et élever le mouton en Australie...' and examples of French settlers who prospered by becoming shepherds/farmers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages emigrants to follow global agricultural opportunities rather than remaining confined to France; stresses need for 'une éducation assez forte' to allow responsible capital management and success abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum and public collections as tools for popular instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The museum 'centralise... les divers sujets du règne animal, végétal et minéral' and is described as facilitating public instruction with collections from local flora/fauna, industrial models, and comparative anthropology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public museums should aggregate natural history, economic products, and industrial models to aid education of colonists and visitors; inclusion of copies of classical sculptures and local curiosities (e.g., moa skeleton) increases both instructive and cultural value.
